approvedHook: Your API key is stored in GitHub Secrets. Which code can use it?
approvedCta: Review what your deployment workflow is allowed to access.
narration: Your API key is stored in GitHub Secrets. Which code can use it?
I separate secret storage from workflow access. A credential can still reach code that a job runs.
Our real secret scan workflow declares a read only repository token. Its two actions are pinned to full commit hashes.
That is a configuration review, not a live attack test. Pinning also does not prove a dependency is safe.
In this labeled example, a step receives a secret. That step, and code it launches, can use the value.
I review triggers, permissions, third party actions, and which jobs receive credentials before allowing a deployment.
I keep untrusted pull request code away from privileged deployment credentials. Useful automation still needs a clear access boundary.
I also avoid printing secrets. Automatic masking is not guaranteed to catch every transformed value.
GitHub Secrets stores the value. My workflow design determines how code receives it.
Review what your deployment workflow is allowed to access.
